what_its_for: Hawthorn is an herbal supplement that has been used to support heart health. It may help improve blood flow to the heart, support healthy blood pressure already within normal range, and ease mild symptoms of heart function changes such as mild shortness of breath or tiredness with exertion. It is also sometimes used to support general circulation. Always talk to your doctor before using this supplement, especially if you have a heart condition.
how_to_take: Take hawthorn by mouth with a full glass of water. You may take it with or without food, but taking it with food can help reduce any stomach upset. Swallow tablets or capsules whole. If using a liquid extract, use the measuring dropper or spoon that comes with the product to get the right amount. Do not take more than the recommended amount on the label or as directed by your doctor or pharmacist.
dosing: The typical adult dose used in studies is 160 to 900 mg of standardized hawthorn extract per day, usually divided into 2 or 3 doses. A common dosing schedule is 80 to 300 mg taken two to three times daily. However, doses can vary depending on the product and why you are using it. Always follow the directions on the package or as recommended by your healthcare provider. There is no established dose for children, so it should not be used in children without a doctor's guidance.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store hawthorn supplements at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all supplements out of reach of children and pets. Check the expiration date on the package and do not use it after that date. Dispose of any expired or unused supplement safely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking hawthorn with prescription heart medications such as digoxin, beta-blockers, nitrates, or blood pressure medicines without first talking to your doctor, as hawthorn may increase their effects and cause your blood pressure or heart rate to drop too low. Avoid combining hawthorn with other herbal supplements that affect the heart or blood pressure. Limit alcohol while taking hawthorn. Avoid taking larger amounts than recommended, as high doses may cause dizziness or heart rhythm problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience chest pain, irregular or fast heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, sudden shortness of breath, swelling in your legs or feet, or any allergic reaction signs such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse after several weeks of use. Always let your doctor know you are taking hawthorn before starting any new prescription medication.
when_it_works: Hawthorn generally takes several weeks to notice any benefit. Most studies show that noticeable effects on heart function and symptoms may take 6 to 8 weeks of regular use. Be patient and continue taking it as directed. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your healthcare provider.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should not use hawthorn without consulting a doctor first, as its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been established. Hawthorn is generally not recommended for children unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Older adults should use hawthorn cautiously, especially if they are taking multiple medications for heart disease or blood pressure, due to the risk of interactions. People with known heart conditions should only use hawthorn under close medical supervision and should not use it as a replacement for prescribed heart medications.
